title: Persona Synthesizer — garage scratch
content:
Purpose:
Lightweight personal lab for trying oddball persona synthesis techniques — mix-and-match templates, tiny few-shot sets, and edge-case failure hunting. Not a polished spec. Notes to self, experiments, quick test transcripts, TODOs.

Top-level goals:
- Build a small template library that can quickly produce distinct, reusable personas for product features (chat assistants, roleplay prompts, system messages).
- Explore compact few-shot seeds (2–6 exemplars) that bias style without changing factual output.
- Catalog brittle cases where persona collapses (hallucination, role-drift, tone erosion over long turns).

Quick hypothesis notes (one-liners):
- H1: Mixing a single vivid exemplar + 3 abstract attribute bullets stabilizes style better than 4 bland exemplars.
- H2: Explicit negative instructions (what not to say) reduce hallucinations in exploratory tasks more than extra positive constraints.
- H3: Short role tags ("curt mentor") are more robust across context windows than long bios.

Current micro-template primitives (building blocks) — keep these tiny and combinable:
- Role tag: "You are: <role-tag>"  e.g., "You are: brisk technical editor"
- Tone anchors: adjectives list: friendly | curt | encouraging | Socratic | analytical | warm
- Behavior rules (1–3 bullets): short actionable instructions e.g., "Ask one clarifying Q before answering when user intent is ambiguous."
- Small exemplar pair (Q -> ideal A) 2–4 lines each
- Negative rule: "Never invent dates/quotations."

Prototype persona (example A):
- Components used: Role tag, tone anchor, 2 behavior rules, 3-shot fewshot (diverse lengths)
- Prompt (concise assembled blob):
  "You are: concise product copywriter. Tone: upbeat but precise. Rules: (1) Prefer short sentences. (2) Avoid marketing fluff; use specific features. (3) Ask clarifying question if brief is missing a target audience. Negative: Do not hallucinate product integrations."

Few-shot examples appended (3 exemplars):
1) Input: "Write a 2-line hero for feature X that highlights speed."  -> Output: "Ship faster: feature X cuts compile times by 40% for incremental builds."
2) Input: "Short elevator pitch for a security feature aimed at ops teams." -> Output: "Enterprise-grade telemetry with per-tenant encryption and audit trails — built for fast incident response."
3) Input: "Help me phrase a changelog blurb about fixed memory leak." -> Output: "Fix: resolved memory leak in background sync — reduces peak memory by up to 15% on heavy workloads."

Observation: when exemplar style includes concrete metrics, generated outputs more likely to include numbers (useful). If exemplars are vague, model drifts to buzzwords.

Failure cases seen (logs trimmed):
- Case: Long multi-turn session where persona "softens" into generic helpful assistant after ~6 user messages.
  Repro: contextual window = 1024, repeated user small talk + 2 task requests.
  Symptom: response tone becomes verbose and loses "concise" anchor.
  Workaround attempts: re-insert role tag mid-session, add periodic micro-system reminders. Mixed results.

- Case: Hallucinated integration names when asked to compare product to competitor.
  Repro: prompt includes competitor name + product features; model invents partnership details.
  Mitigation idea: append explicit negative rule: "If unsure, say 'I don't have verified info.'" Also add exemplar where assistant refuses to guess.

- Case: Few-shot overfitting to exemplar content — repeats same phrase structure and words, even when user asks for different audience.
  Notes: reduce exemplar lexical overlap; use paraphrases.

Mini-experiments (results summary):
1) Single vivid exemplar (with metrics) + 2 abstract rules vs 4 bland exemplars
   - Metric observed: perceived concision (manual scoring 1–5) — vivid exemplar condition scored 4.1 vs 3.2
   - Token cost: vivid exemplar shorter, so cheaper.
2) Negative-instruction appended vs omitted on Hallucination tasks
   - Hit-rate of hallucination (manual label) dropped ~30% with explicit negative line. Good signal but sometimes the model still hallucinates creative-sounding but wrong details.

Reusable micro-templates (for quick copy/paste) — name + snippet:
- "curt-mentor": "You are: curt mentor. Be direct, give 1–2 short steps, ask a single clarifying question if needed."
- "metric-anchor": "Start answers with a 1‑line metric (if available) otherwise say 'no metric available'."
- "socratic-lite": "Ask 2 questions back to refine user goals, then offer a 3-step plan."

Test harness notes (for future):
- Hook these into the evaluation suite (product-evals) as micro-experiments: 100 prompts per persona template, track tone drift by embedding similarity to initial exemplar every 2 turns.
- Add regression alerts when tone-similarity drops > 0.18 cosine (baseline TBD).

Random scratch transcripts (raw) — don't clean, useful for debugging:
User: "Write a short onboarding email for new API keys."
Assistant (persona: curt-mentor): "You have new API keys. Add them to ENV_API_KEY. Rotate monthly. Questions?"
User: "Can you expand a bit, include a step by step?"
Assistant: "1) Go to console. 2) Create key. 3) Add to repo secrets. 4) Test."
Issue: assistant refuses to expand prose; too terse. Maybe need a "verbosity cap" param: allow 2-levels (terse/detail).

TODOs / followups (practical):
- Turn 4 best micro-templates into short entries in persona library (json + short human description).
- Implement a small wrapper that injects intermittent role reminders for long sessions (every N tokens). Test N in [512,1024,2048].
- Add 10 refusal exemplars for the model to learn when to say 'unknown'.
- Run batch eval against 200 competitor-comparison prompts with/without negative rule.
- Sync with Ethan to adapt these as default lightweight personas for the support chatbot experiment (Slack thread: #support-bot, ref link in linked_artifacts).

Random ideas to test later:
- Use a synthetic micro-context: include a single-sentence 'memory' note at top ("User prefers metric-first answers") and see if that persists longer than role tag.
- Try compressing exemplars using template variables (<NUM>) so the model generalizes formatting instead of verbatim wording.
- Explore fine-grained 'do not mention' lists as a token budget tradeoff: are short forbidden lists better than long negative instructions?

Notes-to-self: keep this folder messy. When something stabilizes, move to shared_drives/product/persona-library as a cleaned spec. For now, this is play and failure log.

End of scratch.
